title: Candle Anatomy
hook: Body, wicks, open, close. Know every part before you read a single chart.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to name every part of a candle and know which one shows acceptance.

beats.heading: Body, wick, high, low
beats.body: The body shows the distance between open and close. The wick shows where price traveled but did not fully hold. High and low show the full range.

beats.heading: A wick isn't automatically a reversal
beats.body: It means price reached that area and did not close there. Context tells you what that rejection means.

blocks.heading: Label the candle anatomy
blocks.prompt: Tap each button to reveal one part of the candle.

blocks.heading: Build the anatomy read
blocks.prompt: Tap the steps in the clean order for reading a candle.

items.label: Check the wicks
items.desc: Where did price travel but not hold?

blocks.successFeedback: Clean anatomy read. Body, wicks, then close — that helps you separate movement from acceptance.
blocks.failFeedback: Almost — read the body, check the wicks, then respect where price actually closed.

blocks.quote: A wick shows me where price went. A close shows me where price accepted. That difference matters.

questions.question: A candle has a huge range from high to low, but its open and close are almost identical. Is that a large-bodied candle or a small-bodied one?
options: Small-bodied — despite the wide range, price didn't settle far from where it started
Large-bodied — a wide high-to-low range always means a large body
It's impossible to know without the color
questions.why: Body size comes from the open-to-close distance, not the full high-to-low range.

questions.question: Price wicks above resistance but closes below it — that means it reached above but did not ___ above.
questions.why: Without a close above the level, there's no acceptance above it.

blocks.prompt: Imagine another AGHF girl asks: "What's the difference between a wick and a close?" How would you explain it to her?

takeaways: The body is open-to-close distance; the wick is the reach that didn't hold.
A wick shows where price traveled; a close shows where price accepted.
Reading a candle cleanly means: body, then wicks, then close.
remember: A wick shows me where price went. A close shows me where price accepted.
